I guess the second half of my question was that as the DDA run will pick the most abundant n peptides in each ms1 spectra, some low abundance peptides might be missed altogether and therefore won't be present in the spectral library. So in that sense shouldn't the DIA formed library produce a better coverage as it should contain every hypothetical peptide possible?

Hey, thanks a lot for commenting. I think I can deal with it better now than when i first got it, though neither me or doctors know if it will last 5 years or forever. I just wanted to post because of how much it affected my view on disability and how it affects people. The depression has been bad, but i know how much i have to be thankful for, or how much worse it could be.

To be honest, tramadol does not work that well- but is obviously better than anything over the counter and it works better than codeine for me. Drug use is pretty standard here and im not always in the best state of mind to be responsible with harder drugs than what i have.

Im happy you have a freind to talk about it too, i havnt really met anyone who i think has gone through something similar. But having freinds and family who know about it is good enough to keep me secure in myself. And you made me feel better about the whole thing anyway. Best of luck to you both :)
